title: How Consumers Can Verify ISI Marks and CM/L License Numbers
content: Consumers can verify the authenticity of an ISI Mark using the 'Verify License Details' feature in the official BIS Care mobile app or via the Manakonline portal (manakonline.in). Every genuine ISI mark is accompanied by a 7 or 8-digit Certification Marks Licence (CM/L) number. Entering this CM/L number provides: 1) The licensee's name and factory address, 2) Brand name and product model, 3) Current validity status (Operative, Expired, Suspended, or Cancelled), and 4) Indian Standard number to ensure that the license matches the product being sold.
document_title: BIS Care Mobile App Citizen User Guide

title: Reporting Fake or Counterfeit ISI Marks & Submitting Complaints
content: If a consumer encounters a counterfeit ISI mark, a product falsely claiming compliance, or substandard certified goods, they can lodge a complaint through the 'Complaints' section of the BIS Care mobile app or the online grievance portal on bis.gov.in. The consumer should provide: 1) Product photographs showing the mark and label, 2) Seller/shop name and address, and 3) Purchase bill/cash memo (if available). BIS Enforcement Branch conducts search and seizure raids under the BIS Act, 2016.
document_title: BIS Enforcement Manual & Consumer Grievance Procedures

title: National Consumer Helpline (1915) and BIS Consumer Services
content: For consumer guidance, complaints regarding substandard quality, or warranty disputes on certified goods, consumers can contact the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) at the toll-free short code 1915, or through consumerhelpline.gov.in. In addition, each of the 38+ BIS Branch Offices across India maintains a dedicated Public Grievance Officer and consumer protection cell to handle complaints concerning certified goods, hallmarked jewellery, and laboratory testing disputes.

title: Legal Penalties for Non-Certified Goods Under Mandatory QCOs
content: Selling, manufacturing, importing, storing, or exhibiting for sale any product notified under a mandatory Quality Control Order (QCO) without a valid BIS standard mark is a punishable offense under Section 29(3) read with Section 17 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Penalties include imprisonment for a term of up to 2 years, or a monetary fine not less than ₹2,00,000 for the first contravention (extending up to ten times the value of goods produced or sold), or both; in addition to seizure and confiscation of non-compliant inventory.
section: Section 29(3) (Penalties for Contravention of Mandatory Standardization Orders)
